definitions.explanation: The traditional Japanese art of arranging flowers in a disciplined and aesthetically pleasing manner.

examples.japanese: {華道|かどう}を{習|なら}っている。
{母|はは}は{華道|かどう}の{先生|せんせい}だ。
examples.english: My mother is a flower arrangement teacher.

examples.japanese: {華道|かどう}と{茶道|さどう}を{学|まな}ぶ。
examples.english: I study flower arrangement and tea ceremony.

notes:
COMPOUND: {華|か} (flower) + {道|どう} (way, path)

ALTERNATE NAME:
・{生|い}け{花|ばな}/いけばな - more common in casual speech

MAJOR SCHOOLS:
・{池坊|いけのぼう} (Ikenobō - oldest school)
・{草月流|そうげつりゅう} (Sōgetsu)
・{小原流|おはらりゅう} (Ohara)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{華道|かどう}を{習|なら}う (to learn ikebana)
・{華道|かどう}の{先生|せんせい}/{師範|しはん} (ikebana teacher/master)
・{華道|かどう}{教室|きょうしつ} (ikebana class)
・{流派|りゅうは} (school/style)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Traditionally associated with feminine refinement, but practiced by all genders. Often taught alongside {茶道|さどう} (tea ceremony).

[Register: Neutral]
